children: Nomura has maintained its 'Buy' rating on Motherson Sumi Wiring India (MSUMI) with a revised target price of Rs 49, saying healthy revenue growth momentum is likely to sustain, supported by strong vehicle production, premiumisation and a rising electric vehicle (EV) mix.
The company's stocks were trading at Rs 39.48 on the NSE, up Rs 4.34 or 12.35% at 01:12 pm.

The company reported revenue of Rs 40 billion in Q2FY27, up 47% year-on-year. The figure was 5% above Nomura's estimate and 13% higher than the Bloomberg consensus, aided by 25% growth in passenger vehicle industry production and commodity inflation. EBITDA rose 34% year-on-year to Rs 3.7 billion, with the margin at 9.2%, ahead of both Nomura's and consensus estimates of around 9%. Net profit increased 35% to Rs 2.2 billion.

Raw material costs as a proportion of sales increased 120 basis points sequentially to 70.3%. However, this was offset by a reduction of around 220 basis points in staff costs and 60 basis points in other costs as a proportion of sales.

Management attributed revenue growth to higher customer volumes, new programme launches and contributions from greenfield plants. EVs accounted for 10% of revenue in Q2FY27, up from 8.5% in the previous quarter. All three greenfield plants have achieved optimal utilisation.

Copper prices rose 6% sequentially and 54% year-on-year, with copper inflation contributing 12% to revenue growth. The company is negotiating with customers to recover increases in copper and minimum wage costs, with the usual pass-through lag ranging from three to six months. Management expects localisation and cost-reduction initiatives to support margin improvement over the medium term.
Passenger vehicle demand remains strong, although management expects growth to moderate in the second half of FY27 against a high base. Capital expenditure for FY27 is likely to be Rs 2 billion.

Nomura expects healthy original equipment (OE) volume growth, increasing premiumisation and a higher EV mix to sustain revenue growth. It also sees scope for margin expansion through operating leverage, the gradual pass-through of commodity and wage cost increases, and higher localisation.

The brokerage has raised its FY27 and FY28 revenue estimates by around 6% to account for higher volumes and cost inflation. However, it has lowered its FY27, FY28 and FY29 EBITDA margin estimates by 40-50 basis points to 8.8%, 9.4% and 9.8%, respectively. EBITDA and earnings per share estimates for FY27-29 remain largely unchanged.

Nomura has trimmed its target price-to-earnings multiple to 28 times from 30 times, factoring in a higher cost of capital, and rolled forward its valuation base to December 2027 from September 2027. The revised target price is Rs 49.

The stock trades at around 19 times its FY29 estimated EPS of Rs 1.9. Nomura considers the valuation attractive, given its expectation of around 25% EPS CAGR over FY26-28 and return on equity of 38-39%.

title: Motherson Sumi Wiring shares surge 12% on stellar 47% Q2 revenue growth; Nomura retains 'Buy'
